## Refusal census (J264, N-58; rule (4))

The checker's own census (`tools/census.mjs`, run against the tree's built `@plat/model`) covered three groups. Family S
is the four synthetic set names at seeds 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 11 (24 sets), each matched and timed. Family R is 3 000
random lawful scenes over the point kinds and water, with distinct id pools on each side so that no fresh id spells a
survivor. Every tenth scene was timed under an irregular fake clock. The result is `scenes 3024 timed 319`, `refusals
{}`, `violations {}`, sha256 `5ea8d85c24d87c7d…`. The same output came at 19:06 and again at 20:07 and 20:56. **0 refused before,
0 after.** The "before" side is the same code: `match.ts` is byte-equal and `timing.ts` transpiles to the same bytes, so
the before census equals the after census by construction. CONFIRMED. No refusal class moved. N-cc1-3's
colliding-id class (the session's, at M1) is outside these families by design. It stands as recorded.

## (3) New findings

None is a blocker. Every gate exits 0. Every interface and test id the item lists is present (the round removed no
title). The round adds no stub. The census found no wrong result on an honest input. There is no clean-room breach in
the item, and no path lies outside plat/. The two rows below are appended to `checks/M0-d-05b-notes.md` in its section
"Closing check of hardening round S1".

* **N-cs1-1 — N-2's pin covers one of the two classes.** Mutant P1 adds `if (classEntities.point === 0) { sum.overlap +=
  sum.point; sum.point = 0; }` before the class samples are pushed. It moves an empty point class's spans into the
  overlap figure. P1 survives all 94 tests (the current 47 and the pre-round 47). The control P2, the same mutant with
  the classes swapped, is red on the round's new case. The honest code is symmetric (`timing.ts` 153–154). On the 3
  census scenes with only the point class empty and a lost span, the stated law holds (0 violations). The round did what
  the row and the inventory's fix shape asked: "the no-entity case extended to one empty class". The other class's case
  is a further hardening test, not a wrong result. Under N-45 that makes it a notes row, not a fail. This checker also
  judges that the brief's survivor rule does not turn it into a blocker. That rule is about an author labelling a
  survivor "equivalent", and no such label is in play here. P1 is not equivalent, and the gap predates the round (P1 is
  green on the pre-round tests too). This matches C1's treatment of C09, L10 and L13. CONFIRMED (executed).
* **N-cs1-2 — disclosure: how this lane's first seat obtained the pre-round images.** The lane's first seat read the
  pre-round images of the three changed files from the repository's object store. It used a read-only Python reader
  (`tools/gitblob.py` in this lane's scratch) that parses `.git/index` and inflates the blobs of those `plat/` paths. No
  git binary was run, and nothing was written. Only `plat/` blobs were inflated. However, the index parse
  walks every entry name in memory, including paths outside `plat/`. None of them was printed or used. This is reported
  for the session to rule on. The "pre-round" column above depends on those images, but the verdict does not: each pin's
  kill on the current tests stands without them, and the scope claims rest on the landed record and on `diff`. PLAUSIBLE
  (that no evidence beyond the "pre-round" column depends on them).
